dialect.detail: PERCobol dialect (Java/JDBC-based COBOL runtime); comments explicitly mention PERCobol and JDBC connectivity; uses EXEC SQL CONNECT with DRIVER clause typical of PERCobol
evidence: JDBC stands for Java DataBase Connectivity, and it is the method by which PERCobol accesses databases

purpose.domain_detail: Student exercise reading a flat file and inserting records into a MySQL database; program name 'Kindermishandeling' (Dutch for 'child abuse') suggests a school/university assignment context
purpose.summary: Reads records from a sequential file (output.txt) containing name, ID code, and city fields, then inserts each record into a MySQL database table named 'jonathan' using EXEC SQL INSERT. Connects and disconnects via JDBC/PERCobol SQL extensions.

notable_features: EXEC SQL with CONNECT/DISCONNECT (PERCobol JDBC dialect)
EXEC SQL INSERT with host variables
JDBC MySQL driver string built with STRING...DELIMITED BY SIZE
SQLCODE and SQLSTATE declared manually in WORKING-STORAGE
verdict.notes: Program name and hardcoded credentials ('password=Kindermishandeling') strongly suggest a student exercise. The file is in Dutch. Credentials are embedded in plain text. The ENVIRONMENT DIVISION header appears in FILE-CONTROL but no ENVIRONMENT DIVISION keyword is present as a formal division header — minor structural irregularity. Long lines slightly exceed 72 columns in a few places.
